intent.title: Show and hide the docks and panels
steps: Press Ctrl+B twice; press Ctrl+Alt+B twice.
Press Ctrl+\ twice.
Close the Layers panel with its close button and reopen it from the top bar and from View.
expected: Ctrl+B hides and shows the left dock; Ctrl+Alt+B hides and shows the inspector; the canvas grows into the freed space and refits in Fit mode. While editing text Ctrl+B keeps its bold meaning.
Ctrl+\ collapses every dock and the second press restores exactly what was open.
Panels close and reopen from the top bar toggles and the View menu; the status bar reports each change.

intent.title: Command bar with Ctrl+K
steps: Press Ctrl+K.
Type 'wrap' and press Enter.
Press Ctrl+K, type 'insert hero', use ArrowDown and Enter.
Press Ctrl+K, type 'layers' and press Enter; press Ctrl+K and Escape.
expected: The command bar lists commands, panels ('Open Layers' [command.openPanel]) and element types ('Insert Hero' [command.insertElement]), each with its shortcut where it has one; fuzzy search filters them.
ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the highlight, Enter runs it and closes the bar; Escape and clicking outside close it.
Commands that cannot apply to the current selection are not offered.
Recently run commands are listed first.
While editing text Ctrl+K keeps its link meaning and does not open the bar.

params.action: Placed Paragraph in Hero, position 2 of 4.
Placed Paragraph in Hero, position 2 of 4.

intent.title: Set a property or jump to it from the command bar
steps: Select a flex Container, press Ctrl+K, type 'gap 24' and press Enter.
Press Ctrl+K, type 'width 50%' and press Enter.
Press Ctrl+K, type 'border-color' and choose 'Edit property border-color' [command.editProperty].
expected: Typing '<property> <value>' offers 'Set <property> to <value>' [command.setProperty]; running it writes the value to the selection in the document JSON as one undo step.
Invalid values are not offered.
'Edit property X' [command.editProperty] opens the section, reveals the field in the inspector and focuses it.

intent.title: Keyboard shortcuts panel generated from the keymap
steps: Open Help > Keyboard shortcuts.
expected: The shortcuts open as a tab in the bottom workbench dock; the workbench is closed by default and opens with its first tab.
The panel lists every binding grouped by context (anywhere, on the canvas, while editing text, during a drag, with something in hand, on panels) with keys and a description.
It is rendered from the single keymap table: a unit test adds a binding to the table and the panel shows it without other changes.

intent.title: Bottom workbench: tabs, collapse, maximise and developer tools
steps: Open the Keyboard shortcuts tab; turn on View > Developer tools and switch between the Keyboard shortcuts and Document tabs.
Click 'Show or hide the workbench' [workbench.toggle], then 'Maximize the workbench' [workbench.maximize] and restore it.
Make a change on the canvas; close the Document tab.
expected: The workbench shows one tab strip; the chosen tab's content fills it; tabs can be closed.
It collapses to its tab strip, expands, and maximises to cover the canvas area, then restores.
Developer tools adds a Document tab showing the live document JSON read-only, updated after every command; the choice is stored in preferences.

intent.title: Resize docks and panels with splitters
steps: Drag the splitter between the left dock and the canvas; drag the splitter between Elements and Layers.
Drag the inspector splitter; drag the workbench splitter.
Focus a splitter and press ArrowLeft and ArrowRight.
Reload.
expected: Each splitter resizes its neighbours with the mouse and by 20 px per arrow key, within minimum and maximum sizes.
Splitters have role separator with aria-valuenow.
Sizes are restored after reload.

intent.title: Float a panel as a window and dock it again
steps: Drag the Layers panel header onto the canvas and release.
Drag the floating window around; close it and reopen it.
Drag it to the right edge of the window and release; drag it to the left edge and release.
Start dragging a panel and press Escape.
expected: A panel dragged out of its dock becomes a floating window at the drop point, kept inside the viewport.
Near the left or right edge a 'Dock left' [workspace.hint.dockLeft]/'Dock right' [workspace.hint.dockRight] hint appears and release docks the panel there.
Escape cancels the drag and returns the panel where it was.
The floating layout is restored after reload.

intent.title: Combine panels as tabs or stack them
steps: Drag the Layers panel over the upper part of the Elements panel and release.
Switch between the two tabs.
Drag the Layers tab over the lower part of the Elements panel and release.
expected: Over the upper part a 'Combine as tabs' [workspace.hint.combineTabs] hint appears and release shows both panels as tabs of one panel.
Over the lower part a 'Stack panels' [workspace.hint.stackPanels] hint appears and release stacks them vertically.
The arrangement is restored after reload.

intent.title: Workspace layout persists and can be reset
steps: Hide the inspector, resize the left dock, float the Layers panel and collapse an inspector section.
Reload.
Choose View > Reset workspace.
expected: After reload the workspace looks exactly as it was left.
Reset workspace restores the default docks, sizes and panels and says so in the status bar; the document JSON is untouched.

intent.title: Status bar: messages, breadcrumb, size, context, count, zoom and save state
steps: Select a nested element; click an ancestor in the breadcrumb.
Run a few commands, change breakpoint and state.
expected: The status bar shows the last message (in an aria-live region), the breadcrumb of the selection, its W x H, the breakpoint and state, the node count, the zoom and the save state.
Clicking a breadcrumb ancestor selects it.
Every value updates immediately after each command.
